check.population: every construction site of the types the pattern governs
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a constructor, a variant or the composition root changes
check.refusal: the review or the construction test rejects a construction that bypasses the creational owner
check.observation: constructor call sites and their argument counts, read from source
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the creational owner, which every construction site goes through

records.name: Factory Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that moves the construction of an object and its defaults into one function or object.

exemplar.before: const foo = new Foo("foo", 0, [], new Date(), "draft");

records.name: Factory Method Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern in which a base class calls an overridable method to create the objects its workflow uses.

records.name: Abstract Factory Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that creates a whole family of related objects through one interface, so the members always match.
detected_by: manual selection of related product classes

exemplar.before:
const store = env === "test" ? new MemoryFooStore() : new SqlFooStore();
const bus = env === "test" ? new MemoryFooBus() : new KafkaFooBus();

records.name: Builder Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that assembles a complex object step by step through named calls and validates it when it is built.

exemplar.before: const foo = new Foo("foo_1", "Foo", [], 0, false, undefined, "draft");

records.name: Prototype Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that creates new objects by cloning a prepared template and applying overrides.

records.name: Singleton Pattern
records.definition: A design pattern that restricts a class to one instance, reached through a global access point.
detected_by: static global access to a shared service

exemplar.before:
let instance: FooService | undefined;
function getFooService() { return instance ??= new FooService(); }
